record.title: MirrorMoE reports improved pretraining for shared-expert MoEs by adapting the routing space
record.summary: A paper introduces MirrorMoE, a pretraining router for mixture-of-experts models that combines sign-mirrored logits for expert selection with the standard routing probabilities for expert aggregation, then anneals the mirrored component to zero. The authors report that shared experts suppress routing-induced feature variance, while fine-grained experts increase the number of routes that must be explored; in four shared-expert models from 100M to 2.4B total parameters, MirrorMoE lowers test perplexity and improves the average on six commonsense tasks. At 2.4B, the reported changes are 0.67 lower perplexity and +1.64 percentage points in the six-task average. The work uses DCLM data and H100 GPUs; the released recipe identifies one DCLM shard and 90/5/5 train/validation/test split. These are author-reported results at modest scale, not independently reproduced or evidence of frontier-scale gains.
organizations: Max Planck Institute for Intelligent Systems

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The paper reports that shared experts reduce routing-induced feature variance by about an order of magnitude in its analyzed model, while fine-grained expert segmentation increases the route combinations that pretraining must explore.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Across four shared-expert MoEs with 100M–2.4B total parameters, the authors report lower test perplexity with MirrorMoE; for the 2.4B model, test perplexity falls from 21.17 to 20.50 and the average over six commonsense tasks rises from 45.23 to 46.87 (+1.64 points).

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The released author repository includes MirrorMoE and standard-routing baseline scripts for four model sizes, and documents an environment based on Megatron-LM, PyTorch 2.6.0 and CUDA 12.4; code availability is not a reproduced result.

evidence_gaps.description: No independent reproduction or multi-seed uncertainty analysis was conducted; the inspected paper does not report a seed count for the main comparisons.
Experiments cover 100M–2.4B total parameters, H100 training and one DCLM shard; performance and stability at frontier-scale models, other data mixtures, hardware and longer budgets remain unknown.

Downstream evaluation is an average over six commonsense tasks; broader capabilities, instruction tuning, inference efficiency, routing communication costs and production serving were not established.

brief.importance_rationale: If reproduced at larger scales, token- and layer-adaptive suppression of low-contribution experts could help shared-expert MoEs realize gains from finer routing under a fixed active-expert budget, affecting architecture and training choices. The potential is meaningful, but current evidence is one author-reported study up to 2.4B total parameters with limited downstream tasks.
limitations: All performance numbers are paper-reported and were not independently reproduced in this activation.
The models range from 100M to 2.4B total parameters; the work does not establish performance at frontier scale.
The author repository documents one DCLM shard and a 90/5/5 data split. Results may depend on this data slice and training recipe.
Downstream evaluation averages six commonsense tasks; broader capability and instruction-following effects are unknown.
The paper does not report an explicit main-comparison seed count or uncertainty intervals for the downstream averages in the inspected version.
Iteration time is similar to or slightly lower in the reported runs, but no full training-cost, energy, inference-latency or serving analysis is given.
The repository provides scripts and code, but no code was executed and no released checkpoint was independently inspected.
organizations: Max Planck Institute for Intelligent Systems
brief.summary: A paper introduces MirrorMoE, a pretraining router for mixture-of-experts models that combines sign-mirrored logits for expert selection with the standard routing probabilities for expert aggregation, then anneals the mirrored component to zero. The authors report that shared experts suppress routing-induced feature variance, while fine-grained experts increase the number of routes that must be explored; in four shared-expert models from 100M to 2.4B total parameters, MirrorMoE lowers test perplexity and improves the average on six commonsense tasks. At 2.4B, the reported changes are 0.67 lower perplexity and +1.64 percentage points in the six-task average. The work uses DCLM data and H100 GPUs; the released recipe identifies one DCLM shard and 90/5/5 train/validation/test split. These are author-reported results at modest scale, not independently reproduced or evidence of frontier-scale gains.

technical.claimed_result: Authors report lower test perplexity across four shared-expert MoEs from 100M to 2.4B total parameters; at 2.4B they report 0.67 lower perplexity and a +1.64-point average across six commonsense tasks, with similar/slightly lower iteration time.
technical.demonstrated_result: The paper and author repository exist and expose the reported method and runnable recipes. The reported model-quality outcomes remain author claims; this activation did not execute the code.
technical.mechanism: Mirror routing selects routed experts using p=(1−ρ)ξ+ρζ, where ξ=softmax(Gh) and ζ=softmax(−Gh); mirror aggregation weights selected experts by ξ rather than p, so low-logit experts can be selected but contribute little. ρ is cosine-annealed from ρ₀=0.4 to zero, and load balancing uses ξ. This adaptively reduces the effective routing space during early pretraining, then restores standard top-k routing.
technical.regime: Pretraining experiments on NVIDIA H100 using Megatron-LM/DCLM; four shared-expert models from 100M to 2.4B total parameters, one DCLM shard, 4.4B–12.8B tokens and a six-task commonsense evaluation. Frontier-scale transfer is untested.
technical.strongest_baseline: The paper compares against standard shared-expert MoE routing and fixed global linear/cosine schedules for active experts. It reports comparable total training tokens; some no-shared-expert configurations use different GPU counts due to expert-parallelism constraints.

brief.title: MirrorMoE reports improved pretraining for shared-expert MoEs by adapting the routing space
brief.why_it_matters: If the reported effects persist at larger scales and across training setups, routing that adapts how many selected experts materially contribute could help shared-expert MoEs realize the extra capacity implied by fine-grained routing without raising the nominal active-expert count. This could affect MoE architecture and pretraining choices. Current evidence is limited to one paper’s 100M–2.4B models, one released data recipe and a six-task downstream average.
